title: Coordination Between a Rider, the Medical Plan and the Allowance Card
content:
The Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders sit alongside a member's medical plan rather than inside it. A rider and the medical plan's own embedded dental, vision and hearing allowance are ordered rather than added: the rider pays first on its benefit categories, and the medical plan's embedded allowance pays only what the rider left unpaid.

## The rider must be in force on the date of service

The rider held is in force on the date of service of the line the medical plan is paying. It is in force for this purpose where it stands active or in its waiting period. This is read before the line is processed, from the rider's own record — its reference, its standing and the medical plan enrollment it hangs on — and from that record alone.

## Where the allowance card comes in

The supplemental benefit allowance card may then be used toward whatever both have left, on the card tiers that make dental, vision and hearing costs eligible, but never toward an amount the rider has already met.

## The two maximums stand apart

Holding a rider never reduces the medical plan's embedded allowance and never uses it up: the two maximums stand apart and are shown apart on the member's benefit summary.

## A member with no medical plan

A member holding a stand-alone Part D drug plan and no medical plan may hold no rider at all, because a rider is an optional supplemental benefit of a medical plan.

## A member who moves tier

Where the member moves to a medical plan tier the rider is not sold with, the rider is ended on the day the old plan ends and the member is told which rider the new tier carries instead.

## The order stated as a sequence of payers

| Payer | What it meets |
|---|---|
| The rider | Its own benefit categories, first |
| The medical plan's embedded allowance | Only what the rider left unpaid |
| The supplemental benefit allowance card | Whatever both have left, on the card tiers making dental, vision and hearing costs eligible, and never an amount the rider has already met |
